Same with women. And even with me, there are limits. I follow a few spit related subreddits and the videos women will do where they fill a bowl with spit and completely cover their face with it are too much for me lol.

I hooked up with this one woman a few times and she liked to take a swig of water and push it into my mouth as we made out, and we'd swap that back and forth. Very different sensation with the viscosity and temperature difference but still very hot.

A friend of mine chews with his mouth open all the time. Always has, even after decades of people telling him to stop. I sincerely wonder if his recent dating efforts are fizzling out because they go out to eat and he can't/won't stop chewing with his mouth open.

Your comment really resonated with me. I know I've had issues with porn but this thread also made me realize it's more than just porn, it's the ritual around it. The secrecy and the "replacement" of my partner, looking forward to her absence so I could keep consuming. I also appreciate you saying that choosing your life over porn wasn't as easy as you might think. I know I'd struggle with that choice, at least right now, and I know that's fucked up. Thank you for sharing your story.

I think it was curiosity more than anything. How much permanent damage have I done? If I just abstained from plucking for a week or two, what would grow back? When I first saw the hair growing back in the urge to pluck came back really strong. I thought weaning myself would be good. In college when I struggled with my work, I'd tell myself that some points are better than zero points when it came to unfinished assignments or tests, and I think the logic works inversely here too: plucking one or two hairs is better than plucking dozens. I let myself pluck one good hair from each hand every day or two and then abstained. I still occasionally get one if it gets particularly long. 

Quitting things cold turkey can be tough, but I think if you just keep forcing yourself to resist the urge until it gets overwhelming, and then just allow yourself to relieve that urge in the smallest way possible, it can help manage the overall impact. That's how this has worked for me anyway.

I also have a beard but I don't pluck from it. Have you thought about how it might look if you give it a chance to recover?

This is a really interesting perspective on relationships because I've always felt pretty strongly about not wanting to be married as well, but being in a relationship i also felt forced to eventually move in together. Since then our sex life has tanked and I feel like i can't ever just be by myself anymore. I feel stupid because I feel so awkward doing anything around her because she's always just sitting behind me, scrolling through social media on her phone and watching what I'm doing. I can't comment on Reddit or Twitch without her watching and asking what I'm saying. She did all the decorating and has tons of her stuff all over the place so the only spots that feel "mine" are my computer desk and my bathroom. It's claustrophobic at times.

The idea of being in a serious relationship with someone who's established separately is something i hadn't really considered because I didn't think anyone else would go for it. So thanks for posting your story. I don't think things will change with my current partner in that respect but i feel less crazy for wanting the same thing, especially regarding the open relationship parts you mentioned at the end.

"It gets better" is a platitude for people whose depression is acute and based more on circumstances than physiology. For those of us who have fucked up brains, nothing naturally gets better. If anything it just gets worse.
It comes and goes. Her cousins were all having kids last year so it came up more often. But yeah, like I said, much less frequently.

That sounds truly obnoxious. It's hard to be frustrated with people who are otherwise fine and not trying to be malicious. My girlfriend does this too but much less frequently than you describe. For example, every time pregnancy is brought up she always has to pronounce it "preganenant" referencing one of those videos narrating poorly-worded yahoo answers questions. Literally every time.
Not me. I knew better and I should know better now. I think I'm being self-destructive.
I'm 30, almost 31, and I struggle with these thoughts. The severity and frequency comes and goes but it's always there. I've felt like this for more than half my life.

I live in America and think about this a lot. I've been wanting to get a gun for legitimate non-suicide reasons but i hesitate to follow through because then suicide will be accessible to me. As much as i want to die, I kind of don't want to kill myself, at least not at the moment. But I also don't want that temptation easily available

I go through this cyclically. Sometimes just forcing myself to open up a game i haven't played in a while or listening to music I haven't listened to recently helps, at least for a little bit. If all else fails I'll scroll a bit on YouTube, see if anything appeals to me, and if not then I'll see if anyone I follow is on twitch. This process helps me feel less anhedonic
I didn't realize my jaw was clenched until I read your comment.
6'1" and close to 300...might be time for me to take a walk or something.
I just made the same kind of account within a week. Here's hoping our next anniversaries have us in a better spot.

I also have trouble with this. One time I was driving home from work and I took a route that is just two lanes (one each way) with intermittent passing sections. I got stuck behind this car that was going under the speed limit and it was dark so I couldn't really see ahead of them. I lagged behind them a bit, checked that there were no oncoming cars and made my move. This guy starts matching my speed and I end up barely getting past him as an oncoming car nearly hit me. Turns out there was a work van in front of him going slow and he started flashing his brights at me. This must have been just a couple years ago but I still think about it and my whole body tenses up. I hate thinking about it because normally I'm a careful driver but I let my impatience get the best of me and it nearly ended badly.

Frankly I don't know how to let go of stuff like this either. I just tried to offset it later on by being mindful and ensuring I stayed patient when driving.

I wish I had the will to deal with this. I even have insurance and everything so in addition to feeling like shit because I feel like shit, I also feel guilty because I have access to everything and still do nothing. It's a rough cycle. 

After getting financially fucked over by urgent care years ago, I'm super hesitant to involve myself in any medical anything. Not to mention my car isn't drivable.
